analysis: Futures recovered off the 4:48am ET lows (Dow was at a 3-month low, now -0.2%; Nasdaq 100 +0.4%) as oil eased back below $100 and the Treasury selloff stabilized — the 10Y is still grinding higher (+4bp to 5.33%, highest since April 2002) but at a slower pace. The AI trade is rotating rather than unwinding: memory names (MU -2%, SK Hynix -5%) giving back overnight strength while NVDA/AMD hold small gains, and JPMorgan's Mag-7 note (relative forward P/E at a 10-year low) supplies valuation cover for the tech bid. The bigger read is that the yield story has detached from the Fed-data debate entirely — cooler PCE and ~65% October-pause odds changed nothing at the long end, and the French-German spread blowing past 120bp shows this is now a global debt-supply repricing (US, Europe, Japan). Signal vs noise: the 10Y print and the global spread widening are signal; Webull's auto-generated premarket snapshots (MU -2%) are fragile single-source noise worth watching, not trading; today's claims plus Friday's NFP are the swing factors that could either validate the pause pricing or send the long end to the next leg (5.6% technical target per MarketWatch). What changed vs the 4am brief: futures off the lows, oil faded under $100 on recovered Gulf exports, the Amazon-Constellation PPA upgraded to confirmed, and the JPMorgan Mag-7 valuation note added.
disclaimer: Not financial advice — for informational purposes only.

headlines.headline: Futures firmed into the last pre-open hour: Nasdaq 100 E-minis +0.4%, S&P 500 E-minis +0.1%, Dow E-minis -124 pts (-0.2%) — off the 3-month low printed at 4:48am ET. The tech/capex bid is absorbing the yield drag as Q4 opens.
headlines.why_it_matters: The bounce off the lows shows the AI-capex bid (Micron, Gemini 4) is cushioning the long-end pressure so far — Dow futures no longer sitting at the 3-month low turns the short-term risk tell from negative to neutral.

headlines.headline: 10Y Treasury +4bp to 5.33% early Thursday, the highest since April 2002 (intraday high 5.342); 30Y ~5.66%. Q3 logged the largest quarterly yield rise this century after the worst bond quarter since 1994. France's 10Y risk premium over Germany blew past 120bp, the first time in 14 years, as European bonds sell off alongside Treasuries.
headlines.why_it_matters: The story has gone global: this is a debt-supply repricing across the US, Europe and Japan, not a Fed-data reaction — cooler PCE and ~65% October-pause odds changed nothing at the long end, so the multiple cap stays until real long-end buying returns.

headlines.headline: Micron choppy after the beat: early premarket snapshots show MU -2% and SK Hynix -5%, giving back overnight strength, while NVDA and AMD hold ~1% gains and the semis bid rotates toward logic and equipment names.
headlines.why_it_matters: Single-source (auto-generated premarket snapshot) — treat as fragile. The pattern is classic sell-the-beat into sky-high expectations (MU has nearly quadrupled this year); the positive read is the rotation, not a rejection of the $32B in customer cash commitments.

headlines.headline: Amazon's 20-year power purchase agreement with Constellation Energy for 190MW of Calvert Cliffs nuclear capacity (online 2030-2032) is now confirmed by a second outlet; Constellation (CEG) +3% in premarket after finishing among Wednesday's top S&P 500 gainers (+2.83%) on the same theme.
headlines.why_it_matters: The hyperscaler-nuclear-for-AI theme keeps building concrete demand visibility — a sector tailwind for independent power producers; for AMZN it is data-center cost planning, not a same-day stock mover.

headlines.headline: JPMorgan cut its Tesla price target to $415 from $445 (neutral rating); shares fell 1.3% Tuesday to $352.84 on 39% below-average volume. Consensus rating is Hold with a $410.98 target.
headlines.why_it_matters: Single-source re-report — treat as fragile. A PT below consensus keeps the China-competition overhang visible, but the light-volume decline reads more like drift than conviction selling.

headlines.headline: Oil faded back below $100 (Brent ~$98 early Asia, WTI $90.35, -0.1%) as Gulf crude exports recovered to ~23.3m bpd — in line with the 2025 average per Goldman — and Saudi Arabia resumed Yanbu tanker loadings. Two Reuters sources say OPEC+ is likely to hold November output targets steady at Sunday's meeting.
headlines.why_it_matters: Recovering supply takes one leg out from under the inflation-fears bid in yields — but the market is one headline from repricing, and the Brent-WTI spread at its widest in four months shows the geopolitical risk premium lingering.

headlines.headline: JPMorgan equity strategy (Mislav Matejka) says the Mag-7 de-rating has 'largely run its course': the group's 12-month forward P/E versus the market sits about one standard deviation below its historical median, a 10-year low.
headlines.why_it_matters: Valuation cover for the tech bid — if the relative multiple has finished resetting, the AI-capex narrative carries more of the tape, though the bank concedes some compression is justified by rising leverage and AI capex.

headlines.headline: Nvidia pays its quarterly dividend today ($0.25, $1.00 annualized; ex-date Sep 10) and is ~flat in premarket; Monday's $150B buyback expansion and Micron's $32B in customer cash commitments keep the AI-hardware tape bid.
headlines.why_it_matters: Cash returns plus funded customer demand are the twin supports under the AI trade — NVDA flat on a day like this is absorption of yesterday's strength, not weakness.

ISM manufacturing PMI at 10am ET (consensus 54.9) and construction spending — growth-and-inflation mix feeds the long-end story.

Can the Nasdaq's AI-capex bid hold into the open with the 10Y at 5.33% and France-German spreads at 14-year wides? Dow futures off the 3-month low is the improving risk tell.
